title: CARE – Coaching for parents to enhance outcomes of an intensive interdisciplinary pediatric pain treatment
summary:
Chronic pain is a common and disabling health problem among children and adolescents. The best treatment available to them is an intensive interdisciplinary pain treatment. During their inpatient stay, patients work with an multiprofessional team to acquire strategies to cope with their pain, with the goal of resuming their daily routines.

For most parents, dealing with their child’s pain is challenging. However, parents play an important role in maintaining and treating the pain. They can significantly influence their child’s experience of pain through their behavior: For example, overprotective behavior can intensify their child’s pain, whereas supporting the child in actively managing pain (e. g., encouraging to do sports) can reduce it. In turn, the child’s chronic pain can burden the family system, e. g., by negatively affecting the parents’ mental health. Due to this close interplay between the child’s chronic pain and the parents, it is important to include parents in the paediatric pain treatment to support the child in coping with the pain and to ensure their own self-care.

This is where the CARE project comes in: A newly developed parent program for parents of children and adolescents with chronic pain should be implemented as an addition to the intensive interdisciplinary pain treatment . So far, the pain treatment at the German Paediatric Pain Centre includes the parents by one weekly consultation with a healthcare professional, the parent, and the child/adolescent. The new parents’ program adds four modules specifically for parents: Alongside the paediatric pain treatment of their child, parents have the opportunity to participate at two online workshops as part of small parent groups, led by healthcare professional with experience in pain treatment. Additionally, parents can refresh their knowledge in two online booster sessions one and three months after discharge. Again, the booster sessions consist of small groups of parents, led by healthcare professional with experience in pain treatment. These four additional modules focus on providing information about their child’s pain condition. Parents should learn how they can support their child in actively managing pain in everyday life.

The effectiveness of the new parent program, in addition to the regular pain treatment, will be evaluated in comparison to standard care. Therefore, families will be randomly allocated to either the control group (standard care without parent program) or the intervention group (standard care + parent program). To evaluate the effectiveness of the parent program, families participate in five online surveys: 1) at the inpatient admission, 2) at the inpatient discharge, 3) one month, 4) three months and 5) six months after discharge.

Questionnaires are used to assess the impact of parenting a child with chronic pain, treatment satisfaction, the implementation of treatment goals, pain characteristics, the self-efficacy as well as the functional and emotional impairment of the children. In addition, open questions are asked to assess the impact of and the satisfaction with the parent program.

The study is being conducted at the Vestische Children and Adolescent Clinic in Datteln. In total, data of 78 families should be collected to evaluate the newly developed parent program. Due to an expected dropout rate of 20%, 94 families will be recruited. To gain a deeper insight into parents’ experiences with the parent program, qualitative semi-structured interviews will be conducted with 10 parents from the intervention group. These interviews will take place after the final module of the parent program, between the fourth and fifth time point.

It is presumed that the new parent program has a positive effect on the impact of parenting a child with chronic pain, the treatment satisfaction, the implementation of treatment goals, pain characteristics, the child’s self-efficacy, and the functional and emotional impairment of the child.
conditions: Chronic pain disorder with somatic and psychological factors

interventions.name:
Intervention group: 
Receiving the newly developed parent program in addition to standard care after baseline assessment (T0: inpatient admission of child).

Control group: 
Receiving standard care after baseline assessment (T0: inpatient admission of child).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Inclusion criteria (parents):
- Parents of children and adolescents
    - between 8 and 17 years,
    - with chronic pain (ICD-10: F45.40 and F45.41)
    - who are admitted for inpatient pain treatment at the German Paediatric Pain Centre
- Sufficient German language and reading comprehension (clinical evaluation)
- Consent to participate in the study

Inclusion criteria for children and adolescents (patients)
- Children and adolescents
    - between 8 and 17 years,
    - with chronic pain (ICD-10: F45.40 and F45.41)
    - who are admitted for inpatient pain treatment at the German Paediatric Pain Centre
- Sufficient German language and reading comprehension (clinical evaluation)
- Consent to participate in the study
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion criteria for parents and children/adolescents (patients)
- Withdrawal of consent to participate in the study
